name: Rome
intro: Two thousand years of history on every corner: the Colosseum, Baroque piazzas and the Vatican. The centre is compact and best on foot; the metro is small, buses fill the gaps.

transit.card: Contactless bank card or 100-minute BIT ticket
transit.note: The metro has only three lines; buses and walking cover the historic centre.

sources: Written from general knowledge for the MVP; needs a human review before launch

areas.name: Pantheon & Piazza Navona
areas.blurb: Baroque squares, the Pantheon and the old Jewish quarter.

areas.name: Trevi & Spanish Steps
areas.blurb: Famous fountain, the Steps and shopping streets.

areas.name: Villa Borghese & Piazza del Popolo
areas.blurb: Rome's central park and its galleries.

areas.name: Vatican & Castel Sant'Angelo
areas.blurb: St Peter's, the Sistine Chapel and the papal castle.

areas.name: Trastevere & Janiculum
areas.blurb: Ivy-covered lanes and the best free viewpoint.

areas.name: Aventine & Testaccio
areas.blurb: Orange garden, the famous keyhole and a food market.

pois.name: Colosseum
pois.costNote: One ticket covers Colosseum, Forum and Palatine
pois.why: The 2,000-year-old amphitheatre where 50,000 Romans watched gladiators.
pois.kid: Find the holes in the stone where metal clamps were stolen in the Middle Ages.
pois.tip: Tickets are timed and sell out: book on the official site, not resellers.

pois.name: Roman Forum
pois.why: The ruined centre of ancient Rome: temples, arches and the senate house.
pois.kid: Stand where Julius Caesar was cremated (the Temple of Caesar).
pois.tip: Little shade: bring hats and water. Uneven ground.

pois.name: Palatine Hill
pois.why: The hill of the emperors' palaces, with a terrace over the Forum.
pois.kid: Romulus founded Rome here, says the legend.

pois.name: Capitoline Hill & Museums
pois.why: Michelangelo's square and the world's oldest public museum, with the she-wolf statue.
pois.kid: Find the giant marble head and hand of Emperor Constantine in the courtyard.
pois.tip: The square and the view over the Forum from behind the building are free.

pois.name: Vittoriano terrace
pois.why: The huge white monument; its terraces look over the Forum and the city.
pois.kid: It's nicknamed 'the typewriter': can you see why?
pois.tip: A glass lift to the roof costs extra; the lower terraces are free.

pois.name: Pantheon
pois.why: A 2,000-year-old temple with a hole in the dome open to the sky.
pois.kid: What happens when it rains through the hole? Look for the drains in the floor.

pois.name: Piazza Navona
pois.why: An oval Baroque square on the site of an ancient stadium, with Bernini's Four Rivers fountain.
pois.kid: Find the four river gods: Nile, Ganges, Danube and Río de la Plata.
pois.tip: Eat one street away; cafés on the square are expensive.

pois.name: Campo de' Fiori market
pois.why: A lively morning market square of fruit, flowers and spices.
pois.kid: Look up at the hooded statue of Giordano Bruno.

pois.name: Jewish Ghetto & Turtle Fountain
pois.why: One of Europe's oldest Jewish quarters, with fried artichoke restaurants and the Turtle Fountain.
pois.kid: Count the bronze turtles on the fountain.

pois.name: Largo di Torre Argentina
pois.why: Sunken temple ruins where Caesar was killed, now home to a cat sanctuary.
pois.kid: Count the cats sleeping on the ancient columns.

pois.name: Trevi Fountain
pois.why: Rome's biggest Baroque fountain. A coin thrown over your shoulder means you'll return.
pois.kid: Throw a coin with your right hand over your left shoulder.
pois.tip: Least crowded before 9:00 or late at night.

pois.name: Spanish Steps
pois.why: 135 wide steps from the boat fountain up to the Trinità dei Monti church.
pois.kid: The fountain at the bottom is shaped like a sinking boat.
pois.tip: Sitting on the steps is not allowed.

pois.name: Pincio terrace
pois.why: A terrace above Piazza del Popolo with a sunset view to St Peter's dome.
pois.kid: Find the water clock in the park behind the terrace.

pois.name: Piazza del Popolo
pois.why: A huge square with an obelisk and twin churches.

pois.name: Borghese Gallery
pois.why: Bernini's marble statues and Caravaggio's paintings in a park villa.
pois.kid: In 'Apollo and Daphne' her fingers turn into leaves.
pois.tip: Booking is compulsory, in two-hour time slots.

pois.name: Villa Borghese gardens
pois.why: Rome's central park: rent a bike or a family pedal cart, or row on the small lake.
pois.kid: Row a boat around the little temple on the lake.

pois.name: Bioparco zoo
pois.why: Rome's zoo inside Villa Borghese.

pois.name: Explora children's museum
pois.why: Hands-on museum for under-12s with play-sized city streets.
pois.tip: Visits run in timed sessions: book ahead.

pois.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
pois.why: Miles of papal collections ending in Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling.
pois.kid: Find God's finger almost touching Adam's in the ceiling.
pois.tip: Book on the official site. Open some last Sundays of the month free; queues are huge then.

pois.name: St Peter's Basilica
pois.why: The world's largest church, with Michelangelo's dome and Pietà.
pois.kid: Climb the dome: the last part squeezes between the inner and outer shell.
pois.tip: Shoulders and knees covered. Security queue is shortest before 8:30.

pois.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
pois.why: Hadrian's tomb turned papal fortress, with a rooftop view to St Peter's.
pois.kid: Find the secret passage the popes used to escape from the Vatican.

pois.name: Santa Maria in Trastevere
pois.why: One of Rome's oldest churches, glowing with gold mosaics.

pois.name: Trastevere lanes
pois.why: Cobbled streets with ivy-covered walls and small trattorias.
pois.tip: Best in the late afternoon and evening.

pois.name: Janiculum Hill terrace
pois.why: Rome's widest free view. A cannon fires every day at noon.
pois.kid: Be there at 12:00 for the cannon. Puppet shows run on some weekends.

pois.name: Mouth of Truth
pois.why: A stone face said to bite the hands of liars.
pois.kid: Put your hand in the mouth and tell the truth!

pois.name: Circus Maximus
pois.why: The grassy valley of the ancient chariot-racing track.
pois.kid: Race each other along the old track.

pois.name: Orange Garden
pois.why: A garden of orange trees with a terrace over the river and the domes.

pois.name: Aventine Keyhole
pois.why: Look through a gate's keyhole to see St Peter's dome perfectly framed.
pois.kid: Peek through: three countries in one view (Malta, Italy, the Vatican).

pois.name: Pizza by the slice (Campo de' Fiori)
pois.why: Bakeries around Campo de' Fiori sell pizza al taglio by weight: quick and cheap.
pois.tip: Point at the slice you want and say how big.

pois.name: Pizza al taglio near the Vatican
pois.why: Creative pizza slices near Cipro metro, a good stop after the museums.

pois.name: Monti trattorias
pois.why: The village-like district just above the Forum, full of trattorias and cafés.
pois.tip: Better value than the streets right next to the Colosseum.

pois.name: Trastevere trattorias
pois.why: Roman classics such as cacio e pepe and carbonara in family trattorias.
pois.tip: Many open for lunch 12:30–15:00 and dinner from 19:30.

pois.name: Testaccio Market
pois.why: A covered market with street-food stalls loved by locals.

pois.name: Lunch near Trevi (Via dei Crociferi)
pois.why: Side streets a few minutes from the fountain with simpler, cheaper places.
pois.tip: Avoid menus with photos right on the square.

dayTrips.name: Ostia Antica
dayTrips.from: Roma–Lido train from Porta San Paolo (Piramide metro)
dayTrips.why: Ancient Rome's port town: whole streets, houses, a theatre and mosaics, with far fewer crowds than the Forum.
dayTrips.tip: Closed on Mondays. Bring a picnic; shade is limited.

dayTrips.name: Tivoli (Villa d'Este)
dayTrips.from: Regional train from Roma Tiburtina to Tivoli, then a 15-minute walk
dayTrips.why: A Renaissance garden with hundreds of fountains, plus Hadrian's Villa nearby.
dayTrips.tip: Check the opening hours of Villa d'Este before you go.

dayTrips.name: Orvieto
dayTrips.from: Train from Roma Termini, then the funicular up to town
dayTrips.why: A hill town on a cliff of volcanic rock with a striped cathedral.

dayTrips.name: Florence
dayTrips.from: High-speed train from Roma Termini to Firenze Santa Maria Novella
dayTrips.why: The Renaissance city of the Duomo, the Uffizi and Ponte Vecchio, as a long day.
dayTrips.tip: Book high-speed trains ahead for cheaper fares.

tips.title: Getting around
tips.text: Tap a contactless bank card at metro gates and on buses, or buy a 100-minute BIT ticket at tobacconists (tabacchi). The historic centre is mostly walking; Google Maps shows bus routes.

tips.title: Dress code
tips.text: Shoulders and knees must be covered in St Peter's, the Vatican Museums and most churches. Carry a light scarf.

tips.title: Water
tips.text: The small street fountains (nasoni) give free cold drinking water. Block the spout with a finger to make it squirt up.

tips.title: Meal times
tips.text: Lunch 12:30–15:00, dinner from 19:30. A gelato in the afternoon is the Roman way to keep kids going.

tips.title: Safety
tips.text: Pickpockets work Termini station, metro line A and bus 64. Keep bags zipped in crowds. Emergency number: 112.

tips.title: Book ahead
tips.text: Colosseum, Vatican Museums and Borghese Gallery tickets sell out: book on the official sites.
